findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The quat sanitizer in the three part sink barely registers a color change on the inspector’s test strip. PIC indicated that the solution is likely from yesterday and will need to be remade. Solution remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Plastic knives are store with the eating and hand contact sections mixed in the consumer self service container. PIC consulted and instructed to store these items so that reaching for the handle of one knife does not contaminate the eating surface of another.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
PIC does not have current certified food protection manager (CFPM) certificate. Ensure sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Open gallon of milk observed in the service counter fridge. Label with date container was opened. CORRECTED- PIC stated that milk was opened on Wednesday. Container was labeled with date opened.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Disposable paper towels observed stored under the service counter handwashing sink. Store paper towels where they are protected from any potential contamination.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Quat test strips are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Chlorine test strips are available in the dry storage/3 comp sink area, but no quat test strips. CORRECTED- PIC found an unopened package of quat test strips in another storage room. Ensure test strips are available for all sanitizers used within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC does not have current food handler training. Ensure any staff involved in food prep have completed food handler training (and work under the supervision of a CFPM).
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training to cover all shifts.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. (C)

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Gravy is 130°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. CORRECTED- PIC turned hot holding unit to HIGH to heat gravy to appropriate hot holding temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57oC (135oF) or above. (P)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Chlorine test strips are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Inspector will follow up on 12/30/2019.
4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

No sanitizer solution observed during inspection. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Made sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Keep a sanitizer bucket on hand during all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. (C)

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC at time of inspection has not completed food handler training. 
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employeed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain ANSI-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. (C)

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-800b Lysol dissinfecting bleach wipes are being used to sanitize kitchen surfaces. Discussed using these types of wipes on non-food contact surfaces receiving frequent touch from clients (door handles, elevator buttons). Kitchen surfaces should be sanitized with a 200ppm Quat solution in bucket with wiping cloth (same solution use to sanitize dishes in triple sink). To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed canned goods, apple juice, and maple syrup being stored on the floor. Ensure that food is stored at least 6 inches off the floor to prevent potentials for cross contamination. Manager moved the products during the inspection. 
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the hot holding buffet area to have pans with food debris in them and used utensils being stored in them. The hot holder had not been in use since this morning's breakfast. 2) Also noted the toaster to have an excessive accumulation of food debris. Ensure that food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized following each use. This will assist in preventing any insect or rodent infestations. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: CORRECTED> 1) Observed yogurt in the tabletop mini fridge in the breakfast area to be probed at internal temperatures of 46-50F. There were 10 4-oz containers of yogurt that were removed from the facility. A commercial cooler is reported to have already been ordered to replace this unit and will be in in approximately 2 weeks. 2) Observed an open container of sausage, an open container of gravy and an open gallon of milk in the cooler in the storage room that were not date marked with the date of opening. Date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods with the date of opening and hold no longer than 7 days. With milk, the 7 days supersedes the date on the jug itself. These items were date marked to reflect the dates of opening. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed the gravy in the steam well to be probed at an internal temperature of 108F. Setting on the steam well was turned to the high setting to heat the gravy during the inspection. Gravy should be heated rapidly from the can to 135F and hot held at this same temperature through the service period. Gravy is discarded at 9AM when breakfast is over.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: The tabletop mini fridge has two thermometers in it, however, one is broken and not reading accurately and the other is embedded in the ice accumulation in the back of the unit and not reading accurately. Provide an accurate thermometer in this unit. An accurate thermometer was added to this unit.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed personal foods sitting on top of, and others stored on the shelf above, a package of biscuits for the breakfast service in the cooler in the storage room. The shelves on the door of this cooler are labeled for personal food storage, however, it is full and overflowing into the cooler. It was discussed that it is okay to store personal foods in this cooler as long as they are labeled as such and stored on shelves BELOW food for the public (including below fruit).
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces need maintenance and attention: 1) REPEAT>there is observed laminate shelving paper on the shelves in the storage area on the main floor (cease the use of laminate liner and seal shelving with paint), 2) NEW> some of the shelving in the storage room is bare wood covered by a towel (cease the use of a towel and seal the bare wood or cover with the Nudo board as fruit and dishware are stored in this area), 3) the tabletop mini fridge has an accumulation of ice (defrost cooler), 4) the microwave in the storage room has rust on the bottom of the interior (unit may need to be replaced so that the interior is smooth and easily cleanable).
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the containers that the single service utensils are stored in to be soiled with food debris in the bottoms of the containers. Wash, rinse and sanitize these containers.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the insides of some of the drawers in the breakfast area to be soiled with food crumbs. 2) Observed the napkin holder to be soiled with food debris. Clean these non-food contact surfaces. 3) Observed the handles on the covers to the donut container, biscuit server, etc. in the breakfast area to be soiled. Sanitize these handles with 100 ppm bleach solution at regular intervals throughout the breakfast service.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
1) Observed paper towels in a box sitting on the floor in the room with the three compartment sink. Store single service items at least 6" off the floor. 2) Observed plates and bowls on the breakfast service area to be stored with the food contact surfaces up. Store single service items with the food contact surfaces inverted to protect from potential contamination. 3) Observed single service knives stored in a container with the handles and food contact surfaces up and intermingled. Store knives with the food contact surfaces down and handles extended up and out of the container.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the three compartment sink not to be sealed to the wall. Seal the three compartment sink to the wall. If a wood spacer is inserted between the sink and the wall, make sure the wood is painted and sealed. 
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No proof of FSSMC at this time. As a medium risk facility, you must have one full time employee who has this certification. This course may be taken with any company that has an Illinois approved instructor.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed a gallon of milk without a proper date marking on the container. Any food that is potentially hazardous, ready-to-eat should be date marked with the date the food is opened or prepared. The food should then be used within seven days. This seven day rule supersedes the indicated expiration date. Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Properly date mark foods once they are opened.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Facility is Medium Risk and should NOT be cooling or reheating foods. Observed a half can and a plastic container full of gravy in the downstairs lobby cooler. The gravy remains from breakfast service. Any food that is heated for breakfast service must be discarded at the end of the service period or may be used for personal consumption. Cease cooling food from breakfast service. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) A thermometer is not observed in the juice dispenser of the lobby. Provide an internal thermometer for this cold holding unit.  All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed personal food and customer foods intermixed within the upstairs cooler. This upstairs cooler is used for personal and customer food service. Make sure that customer foods are stored on the top shelf and that personal foods are stored below all other foods. Designate the lower shelves for personal foods with an appropriate sign 'PERSONAL' so staff knows where their foods are to be placed.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The following non-food contact surfaces need maintenance attention: 1) there is observed laminate shelving paper on the shelves in the storage area on the main floor (cease use of laminate liner and seal shelving with paint); 2) the shelf underneath the lobby microwave has bare wood edges (seal the edges of the shelf); and 3) the reach-in freezer in the storage room is observed with significant frost accumulation (defrost the freezer). Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820a There is no three part sink available for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. During a previous inspection, a variance for using the upstairs dishmachine was approved. Follow the guidelines for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing utensils and equipment for the public. Cease using the mop sink (as previously noted) for the washing process. Make sure that the sanitizing solution contacts the surfaces of equipment for 60 seconds. For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used..

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g Facility does not have a test kit available for the bleach used for sanitizing. Provide test strips appropriate for the sanitizing agent being used. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Initially, the operator indicated that dishes were being conducted in the mop sink present in the downstairs storage room. Previous owner was allowed to use the dish machine in the upstairs room for washing and rinsing and then use one of the sinks for sanitizing and one sink for handwashing. No bleach is present in the upstairs dish area. Bleach is available downstairs. WASH (detergent), RINSE (clean water) and SANITIZE (50ppm bleach for 60 seconds) all the dishes that are related to customer service. Use proper signage so that all staff is aware of the ware washing requirements in a commercial kitchen.  All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800d The following food contact surfaces are observed soiled: 1) underside of the coffee spout (soiled with accumulated grounds); 2) sugar container in the cabinet underneath the mini-fridge (sticky substance from lack of washing); and 3) salt shaker (greasy and sticky exterior). Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The counter underneath the lobby customer service equipment is observed soiled with accumulated grease, sugar, and food crumbs. Use a sanitizing solution  when wiping down counters and cabinets that the public will touch. Also, the thick plastic containers holding breads is observed soiled with accumulated fingerprints and bread soil.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment: 750-600 Plasticware containers in the storage cooler (holding biscuits) are soiled from repeated use. Cease re-use of single-service plasticware. Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) There is an old waste water collection bucket underneath the handsink in the customer service lobby. A current leak is not observed. Empty the waste water containers and remove them if able. In the future, waste water from leaks should be collected in a clean bucket that is emptied and cleaned on a daily basis. Do not allow old waste water to sit and provide a water source for pests or breeding ground for molds.  Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120 the lobby bathroom door is not self-closing. Provide a self-closer for the bathroom door.  All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210 Observed a white cloth being used to seal around an old plumb-line in the back of the cabinet underneath the waffle iron. Cease use of cloths for sealing holes. Use foam that is cut flush and painted or another suitable nonabsorbent material. ALSO,  observed the cabinet beneath the lobby handsink to have the start of rotting wood from lack of maintenance to leaks. Repair/replace the damaged wood. 
FINALLY: THE CEILING IN THE LOBBY IS NOT SMOOTH AND EASILY CLEANABLE. This will be address at the next preopening/change of ownership. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 There is currently no certified manager employed at the facility. See notes in General Comments. There is a new owner present at this facility. At least one full-time employee should acquire their Food Service Sanitation Manager's Certificate. Handouts given during the inspection. All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
Observed that the small refrigerator in serving area did not contain a thermometer.
750-140a-All refrigeration units containing PHF shall contain an accurate thermometer.
Provide thermometer in a bove unit.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: REPEAT .830) Obtain chlorine test kit for checking sanitizer.  Dishes and utensils are washed and rinsed in dishmachine upstairs ain Room 201. They are then sanitized in the sink in a chlorine solution.  Purchase test kit to keep it at 50-100 ppm Clhorine.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Obtain Chlorine test kit.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment: 750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.  Replace light shield over ice and soda machines.
